bull_bear.body: Priority on supply security (inventory build) leading to temporary debt increase; long-term goal to reduce debt by 10% annually; no dividends highlighted; reinvestment in global CDCs and capacity.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Prolonged raw material inflation beyond H1; geopolitical escalation (Middle East/Iran-US) disrupting supply; delay in breakeven of US/UK centers; demand mutedness due to high inflation impacting end-consumer volumes.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously confident on H1 visibility; pragmatic on macro uncertainty beyond 6 months; disciplined on margin protection over top-line vanity; transparent about opex drag from new centers.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly treats INR 80cr annual opex of Development Centers as 'capex-like' investment with 3-year lag to revenue, distorting current P&L; the INR 35cr one-off sale was a strategic purge of structurally unprofitable business rather than a demand issue; smaller competitors lacking inventory buffers are losing share to SH Kelkar during this inflationary spike.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Debt levels remain consistent with our earlier guidance" and the company remains "firmly committed to deleveraging over the medium to long term".
- Balance sheet snapshot as on June 30, 2026 shows Net Debt to Equity of 0.65x; fixed assets are split into Tangible Assets 764 and Intangible Assets 531 (Rs crore).
- Priorities stated as improved cash conversion and prudent capital allocation; the deck makes no mention of dividends or buybacks.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Deep understanding of emerging market consumers, particularly in India and other high-growth markets
- Strong customer relationships across multinational corporations, leading domestic FMCG companies and fast-growing regional brands
- Integrated capabilities spanning creation, application, manufacturing and commercialisation across fragrances and flavours
- Innovation-led growth supported by global creation centres, proprietary molecules, patent filings and specialised research capabilities
- A diversified geographic presence
- Leadership in the domestic fragrance market underpinned by strong consumer understanding, deep customer relationships and specialised formulation expertise
- R&D depth evidenced by development of 12 captive molecules over the last five years and 23 patent applications filed, of which 13 have been commercialised
- Network of 11 creation and development centres globally across India, Amsterdam, Hamburg, Milan, Singapore, Manchester, Almere, USA and Jakarta
- Diversified customer base with no single customer accounting for 10% or more of total Group revenue in FY 2025-26 or FY 2024-25
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Successor risk (leadership pipeline and business continuity) — Sustaining business continuity and growth requires a capable leadership pipeline aligned with the organisation's culture, values and long-term strategic direction; mitigated through structured learning and development, succession planning embedded across key roles with identified successors groomed through targeted training, and cross-functional training to reduce reliance on individual leaders.
- Innovation risk — Rapidly evolving consumer preferences and industry dynamics necessitate continuous innovation to remain competitive and sustain market leadership; mitigated through sustained R&D and human-capital investment, dedicated teams of perfumers, flavourists, scientists and application specialists, research into natural and bio-based alternatives to conventional chemical synthesis, and specialised capabilities in plant biotechnology and microbiology.
- Data security and cyber risk — Digitalisation and technology adoption have increased exposure to cyber risks including data breaches, unauthorised access and potential disruption to critical operations; mitigated by identification of critical IT systems, recovery and business continuity plans, layered preventive/detective/responsive controls (firewalls, encryption, multi-factor authentication, periodic security audits) and FortiClient EMS endpoint management — though the Company notes it is not itself ISO certified for this and only adheres to recognised ISO standards.
- ESG compliance risk — As part of the flavours and fragrances industry the Company must comply with evolving environmental, social and governance regulations amid rising sustainability expectations; mitigated through a phased ESG roadmap with defined actions across sites, energy-efficient systems, environmental infrastructure and EPR registration.
- Geographical business risk / revenue concentration by region — Operating across multiple geographies exposes the Company to varying economic conditions and market dynamics, and concentration of revenues in specific geographies may increase the sensitivity of earnings to regional volatility; mitigated through a calibrated expansion strategy to keep a well-diversified geographic revenue mix and a comprehensive disaster recovery framework.
- Competition risk — The industry's attractive growth potential continues to draw both domestic and global players, heightening competitive intensity that may influence pricing and earnings; mitigated by brand equity, long-standing customer relationships, a diversified product portfolio, innovation and a disciplined operating approach with a healthy balance sheet.
- Geopolitical uncertainty affecting demand and operations — Management states the Company reported its performance despite significant challenges arising from geopolitical uncertainty, which weighed on the ingredients/export-facing business and on global operating conditions.
- Regulatory / listing-compliance and disclosure timeliness — The Secretarial Audit Report for FY 2025-26 carries a remark that intimation of a cautionary notice received from NSE on 01 April 2025 was submitted to the stock exchanges on 03 April 2025, beyond the 24-hour timeline prescribed under Regulation 30 of the Listing Regulations; the Board clarified the then-Compliance Officer became aware only on 03 April 2025 and filed the same day. No other qualifications, reservations, adverse remarks or disclaimers were reported, and no significant or material orders were passed by Regulators, Courts or Tribunals impacting going concern.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Mature (India Flavors/Fragrances): INR 1,300-1,400cr steady state. Growth Phase 2 (SE Asia, Middle East): Rapid growth, SE Asia factory operational. Europe: Capacity doubled, restoring double-digit growth. Seeds (US, UK): 3-4 year ramp-up, currently INR 80-85cr annual opex drag, US already has >$1mn contracted revenue.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as "the largest Indian-origin Fragrance & Flavour Company in India" with "a long-standing reputation in the fragrance industry, developed over 100 years of experience".
- Diversified across two segments and multiple geographies: fragrance ingredients feed personal wash, fabric care, skin and hair care, fine fragrances and household products, while flavours feed baked goods, dairy, beverages and pharmaceutical producers.
- Client base is described as "diverse and large", including leading national and multinational FMCG companies, blenders of fragrances & flavours and fragrance & flavour producers.
- Management frames the moat as "the strength of our customer relationships, diversified product portfolio, and continued focus on execution", with diversified presence and expanding capabilities as the platform to participate in long-term industry growth.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Global Ingredients] The Global Ingredients business "recorded a softer performance during the quarter, impacted by lower demand in select export markets amid ongoing geopolitical uncertainty", with revenue shift of -44.7% YoY and "near-term visibility remains limited".
- [FY27 guidance] Management says "the current business momentum keeps us on track to deliver double-digit revenue growth and improved margins for the full year", while cautioning that quarterly revenue pace may vary with the timing of customer orders and margins with product mix, raw material costs and phasing of operating expenses.
- [Exceptional item] The consolidated P&L annexure shows Exceptional Items Gain of 30.0 (Rs crore) in Q1 FY27 versus 2.1 in Q1 FY26.
- [Discontinuing operations] The P&L carries a separate line for profit/(loss) from discontinuing operations, indicating a portion of the business is classified as discontinuing; the deck gives no further detail.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: The Company manufactures, supplies and exports fragrances and flavours, including aroma and natural ingredients, which serve as key raw materials for personal wash, fabric care, skincare, haircare, fine fragrances and household products, while its flavours cater to producers of baked goods, dairy, beverages and pharmaceuticals. Its operating model is anchored in integrated capabilities across research and development, creation, application and manufacturing, run through 11 creation and development centres globally and a multidisciplinary team of perfumers, flavourists, evaluators and application specialists. It operates two primary business segments, Fragrances and Flavours, serving leading domestic and multinational FMCG companies, MSMEs and other fragrance and flavour blenders and manufacturers.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Advance the global expansion agenda through strategic investments across Germany, the UK, the US and the Netherlands, transitioning from a dominant regional player to a globally integrated platform in the world's most demanding markets
- Continue expansion of Creative Development Centres and manufacturing infrastructure/capacities to strengthen innovation capability and customer proximity
- Invest in building the future growth platform through strengthening of international operations, investments in manufacturing capacity and development of differentiated innovation capabilities
- Scale the Flavours business, which delivered strong growth and continues to strengthen its contribution to the overall portfolio
- Embed sustainability across operations and innovation — strengthening ESG integration across facilities, improving resource efficiency, reducing environmental impact and responsible raw-material sourcing to enhance long-term supply security
- Align the innovation agenda with sustainability-led outcomes, with R&D centres expanding the portfolio of natural, biodegradable and compliant formulations
- Maintain disciplined capital allocation, strengthen balance sheet resilience and improve return ratios over the medium term
- Pursue backward integration and value-added offerings in the ingredients business as structural shifts in global supply chains create openings
- Simplify and consolidate the group holding structure by moving overseas operating subsidiaries (Keva UK, Keva USA) under Keva Fragrances Private Limited and consolidating the CFF Keva Italy stake under Keva Italy Srl
- The bundle evidences a formal dividend route rather than a stated philosophy: the interim dividend for FY 2025-26 is placed before the 70th Annual General Meeting (to be held on 31 July 2026 via video conferencing) for confirmation as an item of ordinary business. On balance-sheet discipline, the Company states it has not been declared a wilful defaulter by any bank, financial institution, lender or government authority, has complied with the restriction on the number of layers of subsidiaries prescribed under Section 2(87) of the Companies Act, 2013, has not advanced, loaned or invested funds through intermediaries to ultimate beneficiaries nor received such funds from any funding party, and has not traded or invested in crypto or virtual currency during the year.
- Phased ESG roadmap with defined actions across sites, with continued investment in energy-efficient systems to reduce emissions and improve resource utilisation
- Gradual reduction of reliance on fossil fuels while increasing the use of renewable energy, alongside investment in low-carbon technologies
- Registered under Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) to ensure responsible plastic waste management
- Environmental infrastructure deployed including reverse osmosis plants, multi-effect evaporators and waste-to-manure solutions to support sustainable operations
- Effluent treatment plants installed across facilities with operations aligned to Zero Liquid Discharge principles
- GPCB-approved co-processing and pre-processing facilities for safe waste disposal, supporting controlled emissions and efficient resource utilisation
- Implementation of closed-loop chemical transfer systems to minimise emissions and reduce human exposure
- All manufacturing facilities certified under globally recognised standards including FSSAI, ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, FSSC 22000 and ISO/TS 22002-1, along with USFDA registration; HACCP and an integrated quality/environment/occupational-health-and-safety management framework
- Completed ISO 14001:2015, ISO 45001 and ISO 9001:2015 audits for manufacturing facilities under a formalised Environment, Health and Safety Policy applicable to all employees
- R&D centre recognised by the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) for in-house development of innovative molecules; research directed at natural and bio-based alternatives, improved biodegradability, and conservation and propagation of plant-based raw materials
- Occupational health and safety management system with HIRA, HAZOP, work permits, near-miss and incident reporting and Safety Improvement Programmes; 100% of plants and offices assessed for health and safety practices and working conditions, with fire and electrical safety audits completed during the year
- Nil reported safety incidents in FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25 — no lost-time injuries (LTIFR), recordable work-related injuries, high-consequence injuries or fatalities for employees or workers (including contract workforce), and no working-conditions or health-and-safety complaints filed
- 100% of employees and workers trained on health and safety measures in FY 2025-26, with 56.82% of employees and 100% of workers covered on skill upgradation, and 100% performance and career development review coverage
- Life insurance / compensatory package on death extended to both employees and workers, non-occupational medical and healthcare access including first-aid facilities and group insurance, and transition assistance programmes for retiring employees
- All 166 permanent workers (100%) are members of a recognised association or union, with a Grievance Redressal Policy accessible to all employees and workers
- Value chain partner assessment by an internal audit team covering premises, storage, contingency planning, operations, quality, environment and OH&S under ISO certifications, packaging, personnel, training and ESG, plus verification of farmer agricultural practices for essential oils, with an opportunity report and follow-up against mutually agreed timelines
- Risk Management Committee constituted with a Risk Management Policy, a workflow-based legal compliance monitoring tool, and a Whistle Blower Policy with direct access to the Audit Committee Chairman (no protected disclosures received during the year)
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company is in an investment-led expansion phase, deploying capital across Germany, the UK, the United States and the Netherlands alongside continued build-out of its Creative Development Centres and manufacturing infrastructure. On the manufacturing side, the greenfield expansion at Holland Aromatics has commissioned in early Q1 FY27, while the greenfield facility at Vanavate is progressing as planned and is expected to be commissioned in Q2 FY27; both projects are expected to enhance capacity, support cost efficiencies and enable the Company to meet growing demand across domestic and international markets. In the United States the Company is establishing its presence around a manufacturing facility at Fairfield, New Jersey, and its US Creative Development Centre secured its first customer order and commenced initial revenue generation during the period. European fragrance expansion is backed by the Creative Development Centre in Germany, and the Group operates 11 creation and development centres globally with creative centres at Amsterdam, Jakarta, Mumbai, Singapore, USA, Almere, Hamburg and Milan, plus a Food Innovation Centre established in Mumbai. Under its FY 2026-27 strategic priorities the Company has committed to 'Execute Growth Capex' — commissioning the Vanavate and Holland Aromatics expansion projects while maintaining disciplined capital allocation and financial flexibility. Capex investments are also directed at conservation of energy and resources, including solar power generation units at its units, energy-efficient lighting, variable frequency drives and effluent-treatment upgrades.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management expects the current phase to remain one of investment and transition, with benefits from ongoing initiatives accruing progressively over the medium term and returns materialising over a two- to three-year horizon as new capacities and capabilities scale up
- Favourable opportunities seen across both domestic and international markets, supported by structural demand drivers such as premiumisation, increasing preference for natural and clean-label products and expansion of consumer-facing industries
- Consumer preferences continuing to evolve towards premiumisation, wellness, sustainability and customised experiences, positioning the Company to capture emerging opportunities across global fragrance and flavour markets
- Demand traction in the domestic market for both the Fragrance and Flavour divisions, with the core European business continuing to perform well
- Flavours demand supported by strength in international markets, deeper engagement with existing customers and increasing traction in health-oriented and natural product formulations
- Ingredients business softer on persistent geopolitical headwinds and demand volatility in certain export markets, but medium- to long-term outlook favourable on structural shifts in global supply chains and opportunities in backward integration and value-added offerings
- EBITDA margin at 10.3% reflects the impact of higher operating costs and investments in new geographies, partly supported by operational efficiencies and product mix optimisation
- Industry-level driver: the global F&F market is expected to grow from USD 36.26 billion in FY 2025 to USD 38.15 billion in FY 2026 (CAGR 5.2%) and reach USD 47.31 billion by FY 2030 at a 5.5% CAGR (Business Research Company)
- Industry-level driver: the Indian F&F market, valued at USD 3.08 billion in FY 2025 and estimated at USD 3.15 billion in FY 2026, is expected to reach approximately USD 3.91 billion by FY 2027 (IMARC)
- Asia Pacific expected to lead the global market with approximately 32.5% share in FY 2026-27, while North America is anticipated to be the fastest-growing region on innovation-led demand and premium product adoption
- Threats flagged: rapidly evolving consumer preferences, intensifying competition from domestic and global players, regulatory and international trade policy changes, macro-economic uncertainty affecting demand and input costs, data security and cyber risks, and geopolitical developments impacting supply chains

deepdive.thesis: SH Kelkar navigated a volatile Q4FY26 by exiting ~INR 50cr annualized low-margin business to protect margins, while leveraging superior inventory buffers to gain market share amidst raw material inflation. With European capacity now fully operational and US/UK centers ramping, the company is positioned for a margin recovery to 13.5%+ in H1FY27 despite near-term debt elevation for working capital.

open.item: The greenfield facility at Vanavate is progressing as planned and is expected to be commissioned in Q2 FY27.

In FY 2026-27 the Company will drive operational excellence by improving productivity, optimising supply chain efficiencies and leveraging digital technologies to enhance speed, quality and customer responsiveness.
In FY 2026-27 the Company will accelerate monetisation of proprietary molecules, new product platforms and innovation investments while expanding its intellectual property portfolio.
In FY 2026-27 the Company will strengthen its presence in strategic markets including Europe, North America and Southeast Asia through local capabilities and customer proximity.

In FY 2026-27 the Company will scale the Flavours business by expanding customer acquisition, deepening relationships with existing customers and increasing penetration across high-growth food and beverage categories.

In FY 2026-27 the Company will accelerate growth in core Fragrances, strengthening market share across domestic and international markets through enhanced customer engagement, innovation and category expansion.

As an FY 2026-27 strategic priority, the Company will execute growth capex by commissioning the Vanavate and Holland Aromatics expansion projects while maintaining disciplined capital allocation and financial flexibility.
The Group commits to disciplined capital allocation, strengthening balance sheet resilience and improving return ratios over the medium term.
The Board approved the sale of the entire 17% equity stake held by the Company in CFF Keva Italy S.p.A. to Keva Italy Srl.

Management states the Group is in an investment and transition phase, with returns from ongoing investments likely to materialise over a two- to three-year horizon as new capacities and capabilities scale up.
The Board approved transferring the entire 100% equity stake of Keva USA Inc. from the Company to Keva Fragrances Private Limited in one or more tranches; the transaction is currently underway.
Returns from the Group's current investment phase are expected to materialise over a two- to three-year horizon as new capacities and capabilities scale up.

The Group will continue strategic investments across Germany, the UK, the US and the Netherlands alongside expansion of Creative Development Centres and manufacturing infrastructure to build a globally integrated platform.
Keva Middle East FZE was incorporated in the UAE on 19 September 2025 as a wholly owned subsidiary of Keva Fragrances Private Limited, with the capital infusion yet to be done.
The Board approved the transfer of the entire 100% equity stake of Keva UK Limited from Keva Europe BV to Keva Fragrances Private Limited in one or more tranches, a transaction currently underway.

The Group is making strategic investments across Germany, the UK, the US and the Netherlands alongside continued expansion of Creative Development Centres and manufacturing infrastructure to build a globally integrated platform.

The United States remains an important focus area, with the US Creative Development Centre having secured its first customer order and commenced initial revenue generation as an early milestone in entering the market.

risks.risk: Successor risk (leadership pipeline and business continuity)
risks.note: Sustaining business continuity and growth requires a capable leadership pipeline aligned with the organisation's culture, values and long-term strategic direction; mitigated through structured learning and development, succession planning embedded across key roles with identified successors groomed through targeted training, and cross-functional training to reduce reliance on individual leaders.

Rapidly evolving consumer preferences and industry dynamics necessitate continuous innovation to remain competitive and sustain market leadership; mitigated through sustained R&D and human-capital investment, dedicated teams of perfumers, flavourists, scientists and application specialists, research into natural and bio-based alternatives to conventional chemical synthesis, and specialised capabilities in plant biotechnology and microbiology.

Digitalisation and technology adoption have increased exposure to cyber risks including data breaches, unauthorised access and potential disruption to critical operations; mitigated by identification of critical IT systems, recovery and business continuity plans, layered preventive/detective/responsive controls (firewalls, encryption, multi-factor authentication, periodic security audits) and FortiClient EMS endpoint management — though the Company notes it is not itself ISO certified for this and only adheres to recognised ISO standards.

As part of the flavours and fragrances industry the Company must comply with evolving environmental, social and governance regulations amid rising sustainability expectations; mitigated through a phased ESG roadmap with defined actions across sites, energy-efficient systems, environmental infrastructure and EPR registration.

risks.risk: Geographical business risk / revenue concentration by region
risks.note: Operating across multiple geographies exposes the Company to varying economic conditions and market dynamics, and concentration of revenues in specific geographies may increase the sensitivity of earnings to regional volatility; mitigated through a calibrated expansion strategy to keep a well-diversified geographic revenue mix and a comprehensive disaster recovery framework.

The industry's attractive growth potential continues to draw both domestic and global players, heightening competitive intensity that may influence pricing and earnings; mitigated by brand equity, long-standing customer relationships, a diversified product portfolio, innovation and a disciplined operating approach with a healthy balance sheet.

one-line thesis: SH Kelkar navigated a volatile Q4FY26 by exiting ~INR 50cr annualized low-margin business to protect margins, while leveraging superior inventory buffers to gain market share amidst raw material inflation. With European capacity now fully operational and US/UK centers ramping, the company is positioned for a margin recovery to 13.5%+ in H1FY27 despite near-term debt elevation for working capital.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Steady growth supported by new markets, offset by INR 35cr one-off low-margin sale in Q4. EBITDA/Margin: Adjusted EBITDA INR 83cr (13.5% margin) in Q4; FY26 reported margin 10.2% due to tax and opex drag. PAT: Impacted by higher effective tax rate from subsidiary losses. Order Book: Strong visibility for H1FY27 with secured price increases; no specific backlog number disclosed. Net Debt: INR 851cr (Mar-end), expected to rise temporarily for inventory build before targeting 10% annual reduction. One-offs: INR 35cr low-margin product sale; INR 6cr MTM impact on employee trust; INR 5-6cr depreciation reclassification.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Muted industry demand offset by market share gains; double-digit growth targeted in Europe post-capacity addition. Margin: Confident in maintaining 13-13.5% adjusted EBITDA in H1FY27; long-term target 14% by FY29. Order Inflow: Strong win rates in H1; pricing mechanisms active to pass on RM inflation. Capex/Commissioning: FY27 capex guided at INR 140cr; Almere (Netherlands) fully operational; Vanavate and Vashivali (India) commissioning in coming months.
order book & pipeline: No specific numerical order book disclosed; management cites 'secured business' for Q1 and Q2 FY27 with locked-in pricing and supply contracts; strong win rates in product development pipeline.
segment / subsidiary detail: Mature (India Flavors/Fragrances): INR 1,300-1,400cr steady state. Growth Phase 2 (SE Asia, Middle East): Rapid growth, SE Asia factory operational. Europe: Capacity doubled, restoring double-digit growth. Seeds (US, UK): 3-4 year ramp-up, currently INR 80-85cr annual opex drag, US already has >$1mn contracted revenue.
growth verticals / optionality: US and UK markets (20-25x size of India) represent 10-year horizon; European expansion addresses previous capacity constraints; SE Asia and Middle East driving 3-4 year interim growth.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin ~42.3% in Q4 (net of one-offs); under pressure from 12-13% RM inflation but protected by 2-3 months inventory cover; strategy to pass on costs and exit negative-margin SKUs to sustain 13.5%+ EBITDA in H1.
capex / expansion: INR 350cr spent over last few years; FY27 guidance INR 140cr (front-loaded in H1); focused on completing Vashivali rebuild and Vanavate facility; Development Centers (INR 70-80cr annual opex) treated as strategic capex with 3-year breakeven.
capital allocation: Priority on supply security (inventory build) leading to temporary debt increase; long-term goal to reduce debt by 10% annually; no dividends highlighted; reinvestment in global CDCs and capacity.
risks & watch-items: Prolonged raw material inflation beyond H1; geopolitical escalation (Middle East/Iran-US) disrupting supply; delay in breakeven of US/UK centers; demand mutedness due to high inflation impacting end-consumer volumes.
management quality / tone: Cautiously confident on H1 visibility; pragmatic on macro uncertainty beyond 6 months; disciplined on margin protection over top-line vanity; transparent about opex drag from new centers.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly treats INR 80cr annual opex of Development Centers as 'capex-like' investment with 3-year lag to revenue, distorting current P&L; the INR 35cr one-off sale was a strategic purge of structurally unprofitable business rather than a demand issue; smaller competitors lacking inventory buffers are losing share to SH Kelkar during this inflationary spike.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: S H Kelkar and Company Limited (Keva) is India's largest home-grown fragrances and flavours company, a leading Indian-origin manufacturer with a legacy of over 100 years serving domestic and multinational FMCG customers.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures, supplies and exports fragrances and flavours, including aroma and natural ingredients, which serve as key raw materials for personal wash, fabric care, skincare, haircare, fine fragrances and household products, while its flavours cater to producers of baked goods, dairy, beverages and pharmaceuticals. Its operating model is anchored in integrated capabilities across research and development, creation, application and manufacturing, run through 11 creation and development centres globally and a multidisciplinary team of perfumers, flavourists, evaluators and application specialists. It operates two primary business segments, Fragrances and Flavours, serving leading domestic and multinational FMCG companies, MSMEs and other fragrance and flavour blenders and manufacturers.

capital_allocation.body: Priority on supply security (inventory build) leading to temporary debt increase; long-term goal to reduce debt by 10% annually; no dividends highlighted; reinvestment in global CDCs and capacity.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company is in an investment-led expansion phase, deploying capital across Germany, the UK, the United States and the Netherlands alongside continued build-out of its Creative Development Centres and manufacturing infrastructure. On the manufacturing side, the greenfield expansion at Holland Aromatics has commissioned in early Q1 FY27, while the greenfield facility at Vanavate is progressing as planned and is expected to be commissioned in Q2 FY27; both projects are expected to enhance capacity, support cost efficiencies and enable the Company to meet growing demand across domestic and international markets. In the United States the Company is establishing its presence around a manufacturing facility at Fairfield, New Jersey, and its US Creative Development Centre secured its first customer order and commenced initial revenue generation during the period. European fragrance expansion is backed by the Creative Development Centre in Germany, and the Group operates 11 creation and development centres globally with creative centres at Amsterdam, Jakarta, Mumbai, Singapore, USA, Almere, Hamburg and Milan, plus a Food Innovation Centre established in Mumbai. Under its FY 2026-27 strategic priorities the Company has committed to 'Execute Growth Capex' — commissioning the Vanavate and Holland Aromatics expansion projects while maintaining disciplined capital allocation and financial flexibility. Capex investments are also directed at conservation of energy and resources, including solar power generation units at its units, energy-efficient lighting, variable frequency drives and effluent-treatment upgrades.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously confident on H1 visibility; pragmatic on macro uncertainty beyond 6 months; disciplined on margin protection over top-line vanity; transparent about opex drag from new centers.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Deep understanding of emerging market consumers, particularly in India and other high-growth markets
- Strong customer relationships across multinational corporations, leading domestic FMCG companies and fast-growing regional brands
- Integrated capabilities spanning creation, application, manufacturing and commercialisation across fragrances and flavours
- Innovation-led growth supported by global creation centres, proprietary molecules, patent filings and specialised research capabilities
- A diversified geographic presence
- Leadership in the domestic fragrance market underpinned by strong consumer understanding, deep customer relationships and specialised formulation expertise
- R&D depth evidenced by development of 12 captive molecules over the last five years and 23 patent applications filed, of which 13 have been commercialised
- Network of 11 creation and development centres globally across India, Amsterdam, Hamburg, Milan, Singapore, Manchester, Almere, USA and Jakarta
- Diversified customer base with no single customer accounting for 10% or more of total Group revenue in FY 2025-26 or FY 2024-25

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Prolonged raw material inflation beyond H1; geopolitical escalation (Middle East/Iran-US) disrupting supply; delay in breakeven of US/UK centers; demand mutedness due to high inflation impacting end-consumer volumes.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management explicitly treats INR 80cr annual opex of Development Centers as 'capex-like' investment with 3-year lag to revenue, distorting current P&L; the INR 35cr one-off sale was a strategic purge of structurally unprofitable business rather than a demand issue; smaller competitors lacking inventory buffers are losing share to SH Kelkar during this inflationary spike.

one-line thesis: SH Kelkar navigated a volatile Q4FY26 by exiting ~INR 50cr annualized low-margin business to protect margins, while leveraging superior inventory buffers to gain market share amidst raw material inflation. With European capacity now fully operational and US/UK centers ramping, the company is positioned for a margin recovery to 13.5%+ in H1FY27 despite near-term debt elevation for working capital.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Steady growth supported by new markets, offset by INR 35cr one-off low-margin sale in Q4. EBITDA/Margin: Adjusted EBITDA INR 83cr (13.5% margin) in Q4; FY26 reported margin 10.2% due to tax and opex drag. PAT: Impacted by higher effective tax rate from subsidiary losses. Order Book: Strong visibility for H1FY27 with secured price increases; no specific backlog number disclosed. Net Debt: INR 851cr (Mar-end), expected to rise temporarily for inventory build before targeting 10% annual reduction. One-offs: INR 35cr low-margin product sale; INR 6cr MTM impact on employee trust; INR 5-6cr depreciation reclassification.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Muted industry demand offset by market share gains; double-digit growth targeted in Europe post-capacity addition. Margin: Confident in maintaining 13-13.5% adjusted EBITDA in H1FY27; long-term target 14% by FY29. Order Inflow: Strong win rates in H1; pricing mechanisms active to pass on RM inflation. Capex/Commissioning: FY27 capex guided at INR 140cr; Almere (Netherlands) fully operational; Vanavate and Vashivali (India) commissioning in coming months.
order book & pipeline: No specific numerical order book disclosed; management cites 'secured business' for Q1 and Q2 FY27 with locked-in pricing and supply contracts; strong win rates in product development pipeline.
segment / subsidiary detail: Mature (India Flavors/Fragrances): INR 1,300-1,400cr steady state. Growth Phase 2 (SE Asia, Middle East): Rapid growth, SE Asia factory operational. Europe: Capacity doubled, restoring double-digit growth. Seeds (US, UK): 3-4 year ramp-up, currently INR 80-85cr annual opex drag, US already has >$1mn contracted revenue.
growth verticals / optionality: US and UK markets (20-25x size of India) represent 10-year horizon; European expansion addresses previous capacity constraints; SE Asia and Middle East driving 3-4 year interim growth.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin ~42.3% in Q4 (net of one-offs); under pressure from 12-13% RM inflation but protected by 2-3 months inventory cover; strategy to pass on costs and exit negative-margin SKUs to sustain 13.5%+ EBITDA in H1.
capex / expansion: INR 350cr spent over last few years; FY27 guidance INR 140cr (front-loaded in H1); focused on completing Vashivali rebuild and Vanavate facility; Development Centers (INR 70-80cr annual opex) treated as strategic capex with 3-year breakeven.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).
